VZ.rationale: VZ is a stable, cash-generative telecom with genuine Q1 2026 turnaround signals (first positive postpaid phone net adds since 2013, record EBITDA, raised EPS guidance to $4.95–$4.99, initiated buybacks). However, the stock has already re-rated +20.6% in one quarter on modest fundamental improvement, pushing P/E to 19.8x (73rd percentile of 1-year range) with only a ~70 bps equity risk premium over 10Y Treasuries. The business faces structural headwinds: 2–3% revenue growth ceiling in a saturated market, 2.67x D/E leverage exposed to rising rates (10Y at 4.40%, corporate bonds at 6.1%), oil at $108.64/bbl creating unquantified but real energy cost pressure, and consumer division leadership uncertainty. The quant report's 'Unattractive' verdict is based on trailing data through Q2 2025, but the qual report's Q1 2026 data actually confirms the same pattern: the stock has moved far ahead of fundamentals. A mean reversion in P/E to ~17.5x implies ~12% downside. The turnaround is real but priced in; the risk/reward skews unfavorably at current levels.
key_factors: P/E at 19.8x (73rd percentile of 1-year range) after +20.6% price advance on only +3% revenue growth — classic multiple expansion
Equity risk premium of ~70 bps over 10Y Treasury (4.40%) is historically thin for a 2.67x D/E telecom
Q1 2026: revenue $34.4B up 2.9% YoY, adjusted EPS $1.28 beat, record EBITDA $13.4B, raised FY EPS guidance to $4.95–$4.99
First positive postpaid phone net additions (55K) since 2013; consumer postpaid phone churn below 85 bps in March
FCF guidance of $21.5B+ and 20-year dividend growth streak (~6% yield) support cash-flow thesis but do not justify the multiple
Oil at $108.64/bbl (+76% over lookback) is a forward margin headwind not yet reflected in trailing operating margins of ~23.7%
Rising corporate bond yields (Moody's Baa at 6.1%) increase refinancing cost for 2.67x leveraged balance sheet
Consumer division leadership search introduces execution uncertainty in the core 77% revenue segment
Revenue growth ceiling of 2–3% for mobility/broadband; wireless service revenue guided flat — structural saturation
$5B OpEx savings program and 13,000 headcount reduction support near-term EPS growth but are finite and execution-dependent

Adjusted EPS of $1.28 beating estimates… raised full-year EPS guidance to $4.95-$4.99… record quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $13.4 billion
We are on track to deliver our full year free cash flow guidance of $21.5 billion or more

The Frontier acquisition increased the net unsecured debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio to 2.6x, though management has already repaid approximately half of the acquired debt… $1.1 billion in severance payments during the quarter, reflecting a leaner workforce of 13,000 fewer employees

Verizon's in turn-around mode… Under new CEO Dan Schulman, the company is undergoing massive changes… it needs to do better at the 'basic stuff'
